articles.title: Gusttavo Lima no Camaru 2026: cantor faz oração em guindaste | G1
articles.standfirst: Momento eternizou a primeira noite de shows do Camaru 2026 na sexta-feira (28). Com os fãs acompanhando cada palavra, Gusttavo conduziu a oração antes de retomar o repertório ao som de "Retrovisor".
articles.summary: Gusttavo Lima no Camaru 2026 marcou a abertura do evento em Uberlândia ao conduzir uma oração das alturas em uma estrutura suspensa por um guindaste diante de milhares de fãs.
articles.body:
Foi das alturas que Gusttavo Lima proporcionou um dos momentos mais emocionantes da primeira noite do Camaru 2026, em Uberlândia . Do alto de uma estrutura suspensa por um guindaste, a metros do chão e diante de uma multidão, o cantor interrompeu o show e puxou a oração do "Pai Nosso" com o público. Veja acima.

O momento aconteceu na noite de sexta-feira (28), durante a apresentação do artista na abertura da 62ª edição da exposição agropecuária. Com os fãs acompanhando cada palavra, Gusttavo conduziu a oração antes de retomar o repertório ao som de "Retrovisor".

"Olha pro retrovisor e seja grato por tudo o que você já passou e pelo que você tem!", disse o cantor após a oração.

Gusttavo Lima canta em cima de guindaste durante show no Camaru, em Uberlândia. — Foto: TV Integração/Reprodução

Suspenso sobre a plateia, o cantor aproveitou a estrutura do guindaste para continuar a apresentação e cantar alguns dos maiores sucessos da carreira.

Entre as músicas que embalaram a multidão esteve “Balada”, um dos hits que ajudaram a projetar o cantor nacionalmente. Do alto da estrutura, ele cantou próximo aos fãs, que acompanharam o momento com celulares levantados e muita animação.

Natural de Presidente Olegário , no Alto Paranaíba, Gusttavo Lima também falou durante o show sobre a relação com Uberlândia e destacou a importância de se apresentar na cidade.

Entre a emoção da oração e os grandes sucessos da carreira, o cantor fez a primeira noite do Camaru começar com um daqueles momentos que ficam na memória de quem estava na arena.

A edição de 2026 do Camaru promete ser uma das maiores da história da exposição agropecuária de Uberlândia.

De 28 de agosto a 6 de setembro, o Parque de Exposições de Uberlândia recebe uma programação que reúne mais de 15 atrações musicais, rodeio profissional, torneios leiteiros, concurso de queijos, eventos gastronômicos, exposições de animais, provas equestres, debates voltados ao agronegócio e atividades para toda a família.

A 62ª edição do evento segue com programação até 6 de setembro.

22h Show Zé Neto e Cristiano, depois DJ Netto e na sequência Hugo e Guilherme

17h às 23h Parque de diversões (bilheteria própria de venda)

8h às 17h Fazendinha (entrada pelo bairro Santa Luzia)

Para quem ainda não comprou ingresso, ainda há entradas para alguns setores. Confira como adquirir e os setores nesta reportagem .

Visitas das 8h às 17h, com entrada franca e acesso pela avenida Geraldo Abrão, no bairro Santa Luzia.

Estacionamento: Para quem vai de carro, o Camaru oferece estacionamento pago que pode ser adquirido pelo site do evento ou na loja oficial no Terminal Central. O valor é R$ 60 para quem comprar antecipado. O acesso é pelo portão do lado direito da bilheteria.

Transporte Público: Para quem vai para o Camaru de ônibus, a Secretaria Municipal de Trânsito e Transportes (Settran) disponibilizará linhas especiais durante os dez dias do Camaru 2026. A linha S906 fará o trajeto Terminal Central/Camaru , com embarque na plataforma E do Terminal Central , enquanto as linhas S916, S917, S918, S926, S927, S928, S936, S937 e S938 atenderão o público após o encerramento do evento, com saída pela avenida João Mendes, no bairro Pampulha. Horários e itinerários podem ser consultados no Portal da Prefeitura ou pelo aplicativo UdiBus.

Transporte por aplicativo: Se possível, agende a corrida com antecedência e combine um ponto de encontro com o motorista que aceitar a corrida para a volta.

articles.title: Cantor Mariano anda de toalha pelo camping de Barretos após trailer ficar sem água | G1
articles.standfirst: Sertanejo chegou neste sábado (29) à Festa do Peão para gravação de projeto audiovisual com o parceiro Munhoz.
articles.summary: Sertanejo chegou neste sábado (29) à Festa do Peão para gravação de projeto audiovisual com o parceiro Munhoz.
articles.body:
O cantor Mariano andou só de toalha pelo camping da Festa do Peão de Barretos neste sábado (29) após o trailer dele ficar sem água.

Nas redes sociais, o cantor que faz dupla com Munhoz, saiu do trailer e disse que precisaria procurar um dos banheiros do espaço para tomar banho.

"Amigo, o trailer está sem água, então vamos ter que ir para outro banheiro. Pelado, pelado, nu com a mão no bolso", disse Munhoz, parafraseando um hit dos anos 1980 do Ultraje a Rigor, enquanto caminhava para outro banheiro.

A dupla gravou neste sábado o projeto audiovisual “Balada Louca Duz Munhoiz”, no camping da festa. A resenha com muita moda de viola reuniu amigos dos sertanejos e o público que está hospedado no Parque do Peão.

articles.title: Campanha de vacinação antirrábica em Salvador termina na segunda (31) | G1
articles.standfirst: A ação segue até a segunda-feira (31), com agendamento gratuito para cães e gatos e postos itinerantes neste sábado (29) e domingo (30) nos bairros de Cajazeiras e Cabula.
articles.summary: A vacinação antirrábica em Salvador oferece doses gratuitas para cães e gatos em postos itinerantes no Cabula e Cajazeiras até segunda-feira (31).
articles.body:
Campanha para vacinação antirrábica de cães e gatos em Salvador segue até segunda; confira pontos de vacinação — Foto: SMS

A Campanha de Vacinação Antirrábica 2026, do Centro de Controle de Zoonoses (CCZ) segue com a vacinação de cães e gatos entre este sábado (29) e a segunda-feira (31) em Salvador . A vacina é gratuita e contribui para a prevenção da doença e para saúde do animal e da população. Há postos itinerantes e volantes em diferentes bairros da capital.

O propósito da mobilização é ampliar o acesso dos tutores ao imunizante e reforçar a proteção de contra a raiva. A campanha teve início em 20 de julho e reconhece a problemática da raiva, doença infecciosa grave que pode atingir mamíferos (cães, gatos e seres humanos).

A transmissão da doença ocorre principalmente pelo contato com a saliva de animais infectados, mordidas, arranhões e toque em mucosas ou ferimentos. Com alta letalidade, a vacinação dos animais é uma das principais medidas para prevenir a circulação e transmissão do vírus.

Segundo Danielle Dantas, chefe do Setor de Raiva do CCZ, os pontos disponibilizados neste fim de semana são uma oportunidade para os tutores que ainda não levaram os animais para receber a vacina.

“Estamos chegando ao último fim de semana da campanha e reforçamos o convite para que os tutores aproveitem os pontos de vacinação disponíveis em Cajazeiras e Cabula/Beiru. A Campanha Antirrábica é um período de intensificação, criado justamente para ampliar e facilitar o acesso à vacina, levando as equipes para mais perto das comunidades”, afirmou.

Após o encerramento da campanha, a vacina continuará disponível na rotina dos postos de saúde que oferecem o imunizante.

articles.title: Golpistas se passam por advogados e usam dados de processos de vítimas | G1
articles.standfirst: Golpe do 'falso advogado' atinge mais de 17,5 mil pessoas no Brasil com cobranças indevidas e links bancários fraudulentos. Motorista de Palmas perdeu quase R$ 30 mil.
articles.summary: Golpe do 'falso advogado' atinge mais de 17,5 mil pessoas no Brasil com cobranças indevidas e links bancários fraudulentos. Motorista de Palmas perdeu quase R$ 30 mil.
articles.body:
Informações públicas de ações judiciais têm sido utilizadas por criminosos para aplicar o chamado "golpe do falso advogado". O motorista Luiz Carlos Rodrigues, de Palmas, foi vítima e relata que a abordagem foi feita de forma idêntica à de um profissional, pois os golpistas detalharam dados de um processo que ele movia na Justiça desde 2016 sobre a compra de um terreno.

A fraude consiste em entrar em contato com partes envolvidas em processos reais, utilizar fotos e nomes de profissionais verdadeiros e exigir transferências em dinheiro sob a alegação de liberação de valores de causas ganhas.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

"Eu recebi a ligação dizendo que tinha uma causa ganha por danos morais de um terreno que eu havia comprado e que esses danos morais me dariam R$ 20 mil — R$ 17 mil de lucro e R$ 3 mil para o escritório. A coisa é tão real que a pessoa acaba sendo iludida. Parece que ela é hipnotizada a fazer o que eles pedem", contou.

Seguindo as instruções dos golpistas, o motorista inseriu um link enviado pelo aplicativo de mensagens para fazer um Pix. O prejuízo foi imediato: quase R$ 30 mil foram retirados de sua conta bancária.

Criminosos utilizam dados públicos da Justiça para exigir falsos pagamentos via Pix no WhatsApp — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

O caso do motorista reflete uma prática que atinge milhares de brasileiros. Segundo dados da Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil (OAB), até dezembro do ano passado, mais de 17,5 mil pessoas relataram ter sido vítimas dessa modalidade no país. O número real pode ser ainda mais expressivo, pois muitas vítimas registram queixa diretamente na polícia, sem comunicar à Ordem.

De acordo com o Anuário Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, o Brasil registrou mais de 2 milhões de casos de estelionato em 2025. Quase a totalidade dos golpes do falso advogado é praticada pelo WhatsApp, a partir de dados e nomes reais de advogados extraídos de processos públicos.

Além das fraudes virtuais, a Polícia Civil investiga casos de atuação presencial. Em Tocantinópolis (TO), um homem que se apresentava falsamente como advogado abriu um escritório físico na cidade no fim de 2024, atraiu dezenas de clientes e gerou um prejuízo estimado em R$ 20 milhões.

"Essa pessoa apareceu em Tocantinópolis por volta do final de 2024, se apresentando como advogado. Montou um escritório e, em determinado momento, juntamente com outras pessoas que davam apoio logístico, simplesmente desapareceu da cidade, deixando um prejuízo imenso para inúmeras pessoas de Tocantinópolis, da região do Bico do Papagaio, de Araguaína e do Maranhão", afirmou o delegado Tiago Daniel.

A ação civil tem como alvos bancos, operadoras de telefonia e empresas de tecnologia, solicitando medidas urgentes de prevenção, como o bloqueio ágil em cadeia de transferências via Pix, a remoção rápida de perfis falsos nas plataformas digitais e maior rigor na abertura de contas e linhas telefônicas. Além de pedir a condenação solidária das companhias ao pagamento de indenizações por danos morais coletivos e individuais.

Use os contatos oficiais cadastrados: O cientista da computação Evaldo Reis orienta não interagir com números novos. "Procure utilizar o telefone do seu advogado que você já tem no seu cadastro e não responda a esse número novo que você está recebendo por WhatsApp", destacou.

Desconfie de pedidos de Pix para liberar valores: A Justiça e os escritórios de advocacia não exigem depósitos prévios por links ou chaves Pix para liberação de indenizações ou precatórios.

Confirme o registro na OAB: Antes de contratar um serviço jurídico, consulte o Cadastro Nacional dos Advogados (CNA) no site da OAB para checar a situação cadastral do profissional.

Busque referências antes de contratar: O delegado Tiago Daniel reforça a importância de indicações confiáveis. "Uma indicação de outras pessoas é algo muito válido nesse momento, até porque é uma relação de confiança entre a pessoa e o profissional", orientou.

articles.title: Diretor de handebol joga cadeira contra público em Maceió; veja | G1
articles.standfirst: Clube Alagoano de Handebol informou que imagens foram retiradas do contexto e que o diretor, Ailton Patriota, jogou a cadeira para dissipar uma confusão que estava acontecendo.
articles.summary: Clube Alagoano de Handebol informou que imagens foram retiradas do contexto e que o diretor, Ailton Patriota, jogou a cadeira para dissipar uma confusão que estava acontecendo.
articles.body:
Um diretor do Clube Alagoano de Handebol (Cahan) jogou, na sexta-feira (28), uma cadeira contra o público que assistia à partida das quartas de final do Campeonato Brasileiro Infantil Feminino de Handebol , no Ginásio Arivaldo Maia, em Maceió (veja o vídeo acima) .

Maceió sedia o evento nacional, que começou em 25 de agosto e acaba no próximo domingo (30). A competição reuniu 16 equipes de várias regiões do país na capital alagoana.

A pessoa que aparece nas imagens é Ailton Patriota . Ele arremessou a cadeira após o término da partida entre o clube alagoano e o Esporte Clube Pinheiros, de São Paulo. A equipe paulista venceu o jogo por 20 a 19 e se classificou para as semifinais .

A informação inicial é de que a cadeira de plástico teria atingido uma pessoa que fazia a cobertura fotográfica do evento. Não há informações sobre o estado de saúde dela.

Diretor de clube de handebol arremessa cadeira contra público após partida em Maceió — Foto: Reprodução/YouTube

Ao g1 , Ailton Patriota afirmou que o vídeo foi retirado de contexto e que está em contato com o advogado para se pronunciar sobre o caso . Ele informou que enviaria uma nota, mas, até a publicação desta reportagem, o documento não havia sido encaminhado.

A assessoria do Cahan informou ao g1 que a torcida do Pinheiros estava causando confusão durante a competição. O fato foi registrado no boletim esportivo .

O clube reforçou que não apoia qualquer tipo de violência ou agressão, independente de quem esteja envolvido, e que o compromisso é "preservar o handebol".

Segundo a assessoria, três pais de atletas do Pinheiros foram proibidos de entrar no ginásio por xingarem atletas .

Representante da FAHb (de vermelho) é hostilizado durante a partida entre Cahan-AL e Pinheiros-SP — Foto: Divulgação/Cahan-AL

Ainda de acordo com o clube, quatro pais tentaram agredir um integrante da Federação Alagoana de Handebol (FAHb), que também representa a Confederação Brasileira de Handebol (CBHd).

Por fim, a assessoria informou que Ailton Patriota jogou a cadeira para tentar dispersar uma confusão que acontecia abaixo da arquibancada onde ele estava .

As equipes do CRB e do CSA de handebol, que participaram da competição, além da FAHb emitiram notas lamentando o ocorrido.

Segundo a federação, os pais e responsáveis têm que entender que "o ambiente esportivo é, acima de tudo, um espaço de educação, respeito e formação", e que o compromisso da entidade é "construir uma sociedade mais justa, consciente e responsável".

articles.title: Furto de cabos deixa museu de Cabo Frio sem energia | G1
articles.standfirst: Espaço cultural teve o funcionamento suspenso neste sábado (29) após o corte dos cabos.
articles.summary: Espaço cultural teve o funcionamento suspenso neste sábado (29) após o corte dos cabos.
articles.body:
Cabos de energia são furtados durante invasão ao Charitas, em Cabo Frio — Foto: Redes Socias

Cabos de energia foram furtados durante uma invasão ao Museu e Casa de Cultura José de Dome, o Charitas, em Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos do Rio. O caso aconteceu durante a madrugada deste sábado (29).

Segundo a Prefeitura de Cabo Frio, a retirada dos cabos provocou a interrupção do fornecimento de energia elétrica no imóvel.

Por conta do problema, o Charitas está com o funcionamento suspenso neste sábado.

A administração municipal informou que acionou a concessionária responsável pelo fornecimento de energia para realizar uma manutenção emergencial no local.

Ainda de acordo com a Prefeitura, o expediente padrão do museu será retomado na segunda-feira (31), a partir das 9h.

Até o momento, a Prefeitura não informou se algum suspeito foi identificado ou se o caso foi registrado na polícia.

articles.title: Caminhoneiro só notou que arrastava carro por rodovia ao ser alertado | G1
articles.standfirst: Nas imagens, o motorista desce do caminhão depois de percorrer 50 metros e se dirige até os ocupantes do carro. Caso aconteceu na BR-356, em Itaperuna.
articles.summary: Nas imagens, o motorista desce do caminhão e se dirige até os ocupantes do carro após perceber o que tinha ocorrido. Caso aconteceu na BR-356, em Itaperuna.
articles.body:
O motorista de um caminhão que arrastou um carro de passeio por cerca de 50 metros pela BR-356 , em Itaperuna , no Noroeste Fluminense, só percebeu o que estava acontecendo após ser alertado por pessoas que transitavam pelo trecho, segundo testemunhas ouvidas pelo g1 no local.

A cena, registrada em vídeos nesta quinta-feira (27), chamou a atenção pelo barulho e também pela baixa velocidade com que o caminhão arrastava o carro de passeio, que estava atravessado na via, com duas pessoas dentro, sem que notasse a situação. O carro era dirigido por um idoso de 78 anos.

Um borracheiro disse que o motorista do caminhão parou imediatamente após ser alertado pelas pessoas.

“A boleia do caminhão era muito alta e não dava ângulo para ele ver o carro. O idoso estava atravessando a pista e deve ter entrado na frente do caminhão em um ponto cego", disse o borracheiro, que não quis se identificar.

Motorista de caminhão disse que não viu o carro e acabou arrastando o veículo por 50 metros em rodovia de Itaperuna — Foto: Cedido por Amaro Rabelo

Nas gravações, é possível ver pedestres fazendo sinais ao motorista do caminhão para alertá-lo sobre a situação. Logo após notar o aviso, ele interrompeu o trajeto, desceu do veículo e foi conversar com os ocupantes do carro.

"Como ele estava com o caminhão muito pesado e não dirigia em alta velocidade, quando avisaram, ele parou imediatamente”, contou o borracheiro.

Apesar do susto, ninguém ficou ferido, segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros. Apenas a porta do automóvel conduzido pelo idoso sofreu danos.

O caso ocorreu na altura do bairro Cidade Nova, na saída de Itaperuna em direção a Muriaé. Não houve registro de boletim de ocorrência na delegacia.

articles.title: Justiça determina contratação de aprendizes em Lençóis Paulista | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão da Vara do Trabalho dá prazo de 60 dias para preenchimento da cota legal sob pena de multa diária de R$ 2 mil; ação contra prestadora de serviços urbanos foi movida pelo MPT.
articles.summary: A Justiça do Trabalho determinou que a A.S.N. Ambiental preencha a cota de aprendizes em 60 dias, sob pena de multa diária de R$ 2 mil em Lençóis Paulista.
articles.body:
MPT de Bauru (SP) determina o prazo de 60 dias para empresa de Lençóis Paulista (SP) cumprir cota legal de contratação — Foto: Google Street View/Reprodução

Uma decisão liminar da 2ª Vara do Trabalho de Lençóis Paulista (SP) determinou que a empresa de serviços urbanos A. S. N. Ambiental comprove, em até 60 dias, a contratação de jovens aprendizes para cumprir a cota prevista em lei.

A prestadora é terceirizada pela prefeitura e atua na gestão e manutenção da infraestrutura do município.

A legislação trabalhista exige que empresas de médio e grande porte destinem de 5% a 15% das suas vagas para a contratação de aprendizes em funções que exigem formação profissional.

A medida atende a pedidos feitos em ação civil pública pelo Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) de Bauru (SP). Durante as investigações, o órgão constatou que a prestadora não possuía nenhuma aprendiz contratado e também apresentava falhas no preenchimento de vagas para pessoas com deficiência.

Em sua defesa, a empresa alegou que nenhuma das funções exercidas em seu quadro demanda o cumprimento da cota.

No entanto, o MPT confirmou que diversas vagas se enquadram nas exigências da legislação e que a terceirizada descumpriu o prazo inicial para a regularização voluntária. A irregularidade já havia gerado um auto de infração emitido pelo Ministério do Trabalho em agosto de 2026.

Caso a empresa não comprove a adequação no prazo estipulado, terá de pagar uma multa diária fixada pela Justiça em R$ 2 mil.

articles.title: Congestionamento toma Imigrantes rumo a SP; litoral tem lentidão | G1
articles.standfirst: Rodovia registra 7 km de congestionamento em direção à capital e 3 km de lentidão para quem segue à Baixada Santista. Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes opera no esquema 5x5.
articles.summary: Rodovia registra 7 km de congestionamento em direção à capital e 3 km de lentidão para quem segue à Baixada Santista. Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes opera no esquema 5x5.
articles.body:
Rodovia dos Imigrantes — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/A Tribuna Jornal

Motoristas enfrentam trânsito intenso na Rodovia dos Imigrantes neste sábado (29). Segundo a Ecovias Imigrantes, há 3 km de lentidão no sentido litoral e 7 km de congestionamento no sentido São Paulo.

Para quem segue em direção à Baixada Santista, a lentidão ocorre entre os km 67 e 70, devido ao alto fluxo de veículos.

Já no sentido São Paulo, há congestionamento entre os km 58 e 51. Nos demais trechos administrados pela concessionária, as condições de tráfego são consideradas boas.

O tempo está bom em todo o Sistema Anchieta-Imigrantes (SAI).

O SAI opera no esquema 5x5, com cinco faixas disponíveis em cada sentido. Na Anchieta, duas pistas funcionam para o litoral e duas para a capital. Na Imigrantes, são três pistas em cada direção.

A futura terceira pista da Rodovia dos Imigrantes dá continuidade à evolução de um dos principais corredores logísticos do país, conectando história, engenharia e inovação. — Foto: Divulgação

articles.title: Pakistan hospital fire: 8 officials suspended over deaths of 14 newborns
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered the suspension of eight officials and directed that criminal proceedings be initiated against those.
articles.body: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered the suspension of eight officials and directed that criminal proceedings be initiated against those found responsible for a fire that killed 14 newborns at a hospital in Islamabad, his office said on Saturday.Sharif issued the orders after an interim report by an investigative committee found serious lapses in fire safety and emergency preparedness at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS).The fire broke out on the third-floor nursery on Wednesday, where 15 newborns were being treated. The blaze spread rapidly, and hospital staff were able to rescue only one baby, officials said.The committee found that the nursery had neither a fire alarm nor a sprinkler system. It also said the hospital lacked detailed procedures and adequate training to deal with fires and other emergencies.The report said supervisory staff were not present when the fire broke out. Two nurses, a female security guard and a house officer were in the ward at the time.Emergency services were alerted six minutes after the fire started, while the first responders arrived 15 minutes after receiving the call, according to the interim report.Investigators also found that only two of the hospital's 13 standard operating procedures dealt with fires or other emergencies.“Those guilty of criminal negligence deserve no leniency,” Sharif was quoted as saying by the Associated Press. He ordered departmental and criminal proceedings against officials identified by the inquiry committee.Those facing action include the hospital's executive director, two joint executive directors, the head of the neonatal department, two doctors, the assistant director for security and the head of the Capital Development Authority's emergency services.Sharif also approved action against the private company responsible for hospital security and its officials.The government has announced compensation of 5 million Pakistani rupees (around $18,000) for each bereaved family.The interim report also recommended recognition for a nurse who risked her life to save a newborn before the flames spread through the ward. Sharif approved the recommendation to confer the Sitara-i-Khidmat, a state award for public service, on her.The deaths have triggered public anger and demands for accountability from grieving families and civil society groups.The incident has also prompted wider reviews of fire-safety arrangements at hospitals across Pakistan. Punjab authorities this week ordered an immediate assessment of fire-safety systems, firefighting equipment and emergency-response facilities at hospitals across the province.The fire was among Pakistan's deadliest recent tragedies involving children. In June, 14 schoolchildren were killed when the roof of an under-construction tutoring centre collapsed in Lahore.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Haunted’ Drake’s Island: Tiny UK island with Grade-II listed house, 6.4-acre site, mysterious underground tunnels and 43-bed hotel plan goes on sale for offers above £2 million
articles.summary: UK News: A tiny historic island off the coast of Plymouth, England, featuring a Grade-II listed house, a vast underground tunnel network and former military bu.
articles.body: A tiny historic island off the coast of Plymouth, England, featuring a Grade-II listed house, a vast underground tunnel network and former military buildings, has gone on the market for offers above £2 million, according to The Sun. Drake’s Island, a 6.4-acre landmark in Plymouth Sound, also comes with planning consent for a 43-bed hotel and the potential to generate income through tourism and other commercial ventures.Drake’s Island, located around 500 metres from the mainland in Plymouth Sound, Devon, is being advertised as an “extremely rare opportunity” to acquire a development site with a remarkable military and maritime history.According to estate agent Carter Jonas, which is marketing the property on behalf of a fixed-charge receiver, offers are being sought in excess of £2 million for the freehold interest in the island.The historic landmark initially returned to the market in May, with further details about its potential sale now emerging.Carter Jonas describes Drake’s Island as a rare opportunity to regenerate a nationally significant heritage site while developing new tourism and visitor facilities.A tiny island with centuries of historyDrake’s Island was originally known as St. Nicholas Island, a name linked to a medieval chapel that stood on the site. Historical accounts also refer to the island by the earlier name St. Michael’s Island.The island sits in Plymouth Sound between Plymouth in Devon and Mount Edgcumbe in Cornwall. Its strategic position made it an important defensive site for centuries.In the 16th century, the island was fortified as England sought to protect Plymouth from potential attacks. The original chapel was dismantled in 1550, with materials reportedly reused in the construction of the Tudor fortifications.The island later became closely associated with Sir Francis Drake, the English explorer and naval commander after whom it is now named.Drake departed Plymouth in 1577 on his famous voyage around the world, returning in 1580. He was later appointed Governor of the island in 1583 by Queen Elizabeth I.Drake’s Island continued to serve a military purpose for centuries and was used by the armed forces until the Second World War.What is on Drake’s Island?The 6.4-acre island contains around 30,000 square feet of disused buildings, including the Grade-II listed Governor’s House, a battery and former military buildings.An extensive network of underground tunnels also runs beneath the island, alongside remnants of its historic fortifications.Part of Drake’s Island has been designated a Scheduled Ancient Monument, reflecting its historical and archaeological importance.The island’s military heritage, unusual architecture and isolated position are among the features that could make it attractive to a future owner looking to develop it as a visitor destination.The mysterious Drake’s Island tunnelsThe underground tunnels are also central to one of the island’s enduring mysteries.Local folklore has long claimed that tunnels were built during the island’s military history to connect Drake’s Island with Plymouth Hoe on the mainland, potentially allowing supplies to reach the island’s defenses.However, those tunnels have never been found, and the story remains a long-running local legend rather than an established historical fact.The island itself remains partly unexplored, helping fuel speculation about what may still lie beneath or within the historic site.Island has planning consent for a 43-bed hotelOne of the biggest attractions for a potential buyer is the development potential.The island already has planning consent for a 43-bed hotel, although Carter Jonas notes that the permission remains subject to various planning conditions and a Section 106 obligation.The estate agent says the island has been allocated for heritage-led regeneration, including a new hotel, visitor facilities and research and development connected with the marine and natural environment.The plans are intended to preserve and make use of the island’s historic buildings while introducing new commercial opportunities.“The plans are centred around our committed desire to regenerate Drake’s Island and inject a new lease of life into the existing historic buildings,” the sales brochure states.It adds that the island’s beauty, heritage and location could lend themselves to a “best-in-class development” that takes advantage of its unique setting.Drake’s Island has changed hands beforeThe island was purchased by businessman Morgan Phillips in 2019.It was subsequently put up for sale in 2024, but the property failed to find a buyer.The latest marketing campaign represents another attempt to find an owner willing to take on the ambitious task of restoring and redeveloping the historic site.While the island is currently vacant, Carter Jonas says its past commercial performance demonstrates that it has the potential to attract visitors and generate revenue.Tourism generated nearly £600,000 in 2023Despite its current vacant status, Drake’s Island has previously hosted a variety of income-generating activities.These have included guided tours, private tours, location filming, adventure days and theatre performances, among other events.According to Carter Jonas, these activities generated approximately £590,000 in gross income during 2023.The estate agent says that figure demonstrates both the island’s appeal to visitors and its ability to attract commercial operators.“While the island is currently vacant, this historic performance highlights the significant opportunity for future owners to re-establish and expand a variety of revenue streams,” Carter Jonas said.Drake’s Island has attracted famous explorers and unusual visitorsThe island’s connection to exploration extends beyond Sir Francis Drake.Other notable figures associated with voyages of discovery, including Captain James Cook and Charles Darwin, are said to have departed from Plymouth during journeys that contributed to their place in British history.Drake’s Island has also been the setting for a series of unusual episodes over the centuries.In 1774, local shipwright and carpenter John Day designed a wooden diving chamber and reportedly made a bet over how long he could remain submerged. He died during the attempt, contributing to the island’s later reputation as a potentially haunted location.In 1957, a group of schoolboys staged their own mock invasion of the island, claiming it for Plymouth. They were arrested by the guard but were reportedly given breakfast before being taken back to the city for a double mathematics lesson.In 2005, anti-nuclear campaigners established a peace camp on Drake’s Island and declared it a nuclear-free state.Tours were suspended earlier this yearThe island’s tourism operations have not been without challenges.In May 2026, tours of the 6.4-acre site were suspended while safety inspections were carried out.The inspections came as the island was being prepared for another phase in its long-running history of public access, tourism and potential redevelopment.For a future buyer, addressing the condition and safety of the existing structures would likely be an important part of any regeneration plans.A rare redevelopment opportunity in Plymouth SoundFor a potential buyer, Drake’s Island represents an unusual combination of heritage, development potential and commercial opportunity.The property offers a rare chance to take ownership of an entire island while potentially transforming its existing buildings into a major visitor destination.However, its protected status and historic structures also mean that redevelopment would need to balance commercial ambitions with conservation requirements.The proposed hotel, visitor facilities and marine and natural environment-related uses provide a framework for that regeneration.What could Drake’s Island become?Carter Jonas believes the island could support several different revenue streams under a future owner.Its location in Plymouth Sound, historic military architecture and unusual underground tunnels could potentially make it a destination for heritage tourism, hospitality, events and filming.Its previous commercial activity provides some evidence of demand, with almost £590,000 in gross income recorded in 2023.The challenge will be turning the currently vacant historic site into a sustainable business while preserving the heritage that makes Drake’s Island so distinctive.For more than four centuries, the tiny island has played a role in the defense and history of Plymouth. Now, with offers sought above £2 million, its next chapter could be very different.Rather than serving as a military stronghold, Drake’s Island could eventually become a heritage-led hotel and visitor destination, giving one of Britain’s most unusual islands a new lease of life.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal flash floods: How tea break saved lives of 5 Chhattisgarh friends
articles.summary: RAIPUR: But for a tea break, five friends from Chhattisgarh could have been swept away in the flash floods that devastated the Bhote Koshi and Trishul.
articles.body: RAIPUR: But for a tea break, five friends from Chhattisgarh could have been swept away in the flash floods that devastated the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river valleys in Nepal on Wednesday.They survived, but then had to spend two anxious days watching the fury of the swollen Trishuli river from an elevated spot.Narayan Sen, Dinesh Ojha, Prem Singh Jagat, Yatendra Prakash and Dinesh Singh Thakur, all aged between 50 and 60 years and residents of Mana Camp area in Raipur, returned home on Saturday."We were lucky that we stopped for tea on August 26 when the flash floods struck. If we had left 10-15 minutes earlier, we might have got trapped," Narayan Sen (53) who runs a salon, told news agency PTI."Had we not stopped there, we do not know what would have happened," he said.The group left Raipur on August 21 and reached Nepal the following day. They had hired a car and planned to visit the Pashupatinath Temple, Manokamana Temple and other tourist attractions.At around 9.30-10 am on August 26, they stopped for tea at a hotel in Malekhu town in Dhading district."There we learnt that a bridge ahead had been washed away in a flood. The hotel belonged to an Indian, who helped us a lot and provided us food," Sen said.The friends became eyewitnesses to an unfolding disaster."We saw cars being swept away in the Trishuli river. Bodies and a lot of other things were also being carried away by the current. We were scared. There was always a fear that the flood situation might worsen," Sen said.The group took shelter at a higher spot at Malekhu and spent the night in their car. Local residents and authorities helped them.Thakur (55), a police head constable, said they were around 50 km from Pashupatinath Temple when the flood struck."While having tea at the hotel, we noticed people suddenly becoming restive. Later, we learnt about the devastation caused by the flood. We heard that entire villages, buildings, offices and hydropower projects had been devastated," he said.They later visited the bank of the Trishuli river to see the situation for themselves."What we saw is very difficult to describe in words," said Thakur."We kept chanting Lord Shiva's name, and we feel his blessings protected us," he added.Thakur praised the local administration and police. "There was no electricity and water, but the administration and police helped us. They told us that we were at a higher place and should not worry," he said.The group remained in touch with their families through the internet, and used the helpline provided by the Indian government to share their location."Internet service was working well there, so we remained in contact with our families and did not panic," Thakur said.The friends finally left Nepal on August 28.Amid the tragedy, the five friends shared a tender moment when local women security personnel tied rakhis on their wrists."We were supposed to return from the trip after the Rakhi festival, so our sisters had already given us rakhis. The women security personnel deployed there tied these rakhis on our wrists. That was the most comforting moment," Thakur said.Dinesh Ojha, who runs a tailoring shop, said the scenes they witnessed after the flood would stay with them forever."We will never be able to forget what we saw. Many people were desperately searching for their missing family members," he said."We slept in our car, but we could not really sleep. There was always the fear that another flood might come," Ojha said."We are happy that finally we have reached back home," he added.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Raipur | Silver Rate in Raipur | Bank Holidays in Raipur | Public Holidays in Raipur | Raipur AQI | Weather in Raipur | Petrol Price in Raipur | Diesel Price in Raipur | CNG Price in Raipur | LPG Price in RaipurStay updated with the latest Raipur news. articles.title: ‘One more day, we too would have been trapped’: Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims recall narrow escape from Nepal floods
articles.summary: MUMBAI: 'Had we been there the following day, we too would have been trapped' said a Kailash Mansarovar pilgrim recalled after returning from Nepal, d.
articles.body: MUMBAI: 'Had we been there the following day, we too would have been trapped' said a Kailash Mansarovar pilgrim recalled after returning from Nepal, describing how his group narrowly escaped the devastating floods.Speaking to the media, pilgrim Bajranga Laxman said the group had left on August 16 and was returning after completing the pilgrimage."We left from here on the 16th and are returning today. We were at a safe distance from the floods. Had we been there the following day, we too would have been trapped. By God's grace, we were spared," pilgrim Bajranga Laxman said.Another pilgrim, Sneha Pandey, said they learnt about the disaster while making their way back after completing their parikrama."Fortunately, we left here on the 16th, and while returning after completing our parikrama, we learned about what had happened," Pandey said.She also recalled the difficult conditions they faced during the journey, saying Saga town was deserted and there was no internet access. The lack of communication left their families in India worried about their safety."Saga, which is a small town, was completely deserted, and we couldn't access the internet, so our families back home were extremely worried," she said.The pilgrims' account comes as Nepal continues to deal with the aftermath of devastating flash floods in the Rasuwa Bhote Koshi region.Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), in its latest update, said the death toll had reached 675, while 2,418 people remained missing or out of contact.Chitwan reported the highest number of deaths, with 246 bodies recovered. Nawalparasi East recorded 165 deaths, followed by Nawalparasi West with 63, Gorkha with 57, Nuwakot with 51, Dhading with 45, Tanahun with 35 and Rasuwa with 13.The NDRRMA said those missing included 933 workers from underground hydropower projects, 589 foreign nationals and 127 Nepalis travelling with foreign tourists.Around 18,708 security personnel have been deployed for search, rescue and relief operations. Air and ground teams have rescued 7,514 people so far, while helicopters have carried out 261 sorties.India continues assistance to NepalIndia has continued to support Nepal's relief and rescue efforts following the disaster.Union Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said India was closely monitoring the situation and providing all possible assistance. He said the Indian Embassy in Nepal had activated a 24-hour helpline following the tragedy to monitor developments and coordinate support.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said a specialised Indian technical team had carried out on-site reconnaissance of hydropower tunnels affected by the flash floods to help with search and rescue operations.Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal also thanked countries for their assistance, particularly India. articles.title: Right-wing commentator Milo Yiannopoulos deported from US to UK
articles.summary: The self-styled provocateur had been detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
articles.body:
British right-wing political commentator Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported from the United States after being detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Yiannopoulos, 41, a former editor of Breitbart News and one time political aide to rapper Kanye West, was deported on Friday, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Yiannopoulos, "an illegal alien from the United Kingdom" had been sent "back to his home country", a DHS spokesperson said in a statement given to the BBC.

The self-styled provocateur has called himself the "most fabulous supervillain on the internet" and advocated for stricter US immigration controls. His critics call him a purveyor of hate speech.

Yiannopoulos, who grew up in Kent in the south of England, was arrested on 27 August after arriving at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport.

He flew into the US in May 2019 and "chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation's laws", the DHS said.

He has previously cheered on ICE raids, last year calling for "total legal immunity for ICE agents when they're on duty".

He wrote on social media in 2025: "We have got to deport millions and millions of people. Without that, nothing else matters."

Yiannopoulos also advocated "on the spot deportation for anyone who can't prove they are in the US legally" on social media.

Yiannopoulos was an early supporter of Donald Trump during the 2016 election, headlining an event that year called Gays for Trump during the Republican National Convention.

The commentator has since become a critic of the US president, but still voices support for his agenda. He wrote on X in March this year that Trump had "lost his way, bought off by foreign interests".

Yiannopoulos has courted controversy with his comments on transgender people, Muslims, Black Lives Matter, feminists and gay people, even though he himself identified as gay. He now calls himself an "ex-gay".

In 2020, he assisted West in the rapper's unsuccessful bid to become president. He also worked for Marjorie Taylor Greene, a former Republican congresswoman who fell out with Trump and became a fierce critic before resigning from office.

Laura Loomer, a far-right commentator and Trump ally who has feuded with Yiannopoulos, took credit for his arrest by ICE, claiming on X on Friday night that his flight back to the UK had already departed.

"This subversive foreign agent is already out of the United States and DHS tells me he's NEVER allowed to come back to the United States ever again," she wrote.

In 2017, he was disinvited from speaking at CPAC, a US conservative conference that also hosted Trump, after footage emerged of Yiannopoulos appearing to condone paedophilia. He also later apologised and resigned from Breitbart.

He denied the allegations and said he had been speaking about his own experiences as a child.

Yiannopoulos was once regularly linked with the alt-right, a disparate group that is outspoken against political correctness and feminism, and which includes neo-Nazis and white supremacists among its ranks.

He has said he did not consider himself part of the alt-right, although he has called it "energising and exciting".

articles.title: Flood scare in MP: IAF helicopters, SDRF teams deployed as Mandakini river overflows
articles.summary: SATNA: Two Indian Air Force helicopters were deployed on Saturday evening to rescue stranded people in Chitrakoot after torrential rains caused the Ma.
articles.body: SATNA: Two Indian Air Force helicopters were deployed on Saturday evening to rescue stranded people in Chitrakoot after torrential rains caused the Mandakini river to overflow, flooding large parts of the pilgrimage town on the Madhya Pradesh-Uttar Pradesh border.Three State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams were also engaged in shifting people to safer places, an official said, adding that chief minister Mohan Yadav was expected to carry out an aerial inspection of the area on Sunday."There has been no loss of life....The river's catchment area received 10 cm of rain in just three hours, which led to the situation," Satna collector Satish Kumar S told news agency PTI over phone late in the evening.Another official said a dam breach in neighbouring Uttar Pradesh worsened the situation.Boats were being used on inundated roads to rescue people and six relief shelters had been prepared to accommodate those affected, he said.Majhgawan tehsil, where Chitrakoot is located, recorded more than 148 mm of rainfall between 8 am on Friday and 8.30 pm on Saturday, a Meteorological Department official said.India Meteorological Department (IMD) Bhopal office meteorologist S N Sahu said Satna was likely to receive heavy rain until 8 am on Sunday.The district is expected to receive light to moderate rain on Sunday and Monday, heavy rain on Tuesday and very heavy rain on Wednesday, he added.Satna district public relations officer Rajesh Singh said neighbouring Birsinghpur tehsil recorded 122 mm of rainfall between 8 am on Friday and 8 am on Saturday.The water level in articles.title: Turkiye summons Ukraine ambassador over Black Sea attacks
articles.summary: Two Turkish-operated vessels have been struck this week as a result of the war between Russia and Ukraine.
articles.body:
Ukraine's ambassador to Turkiye has been summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Ankara following two attacks on Turkish-operated vessels in the Black Sea.

Turkish officials communicated their concerns to Ambassador Naryman Dzhelialo at the ministry on Saturday, the AFP news agency reported.

"During the meeting, Turkiye warned about the absolute need to ensure the safety of people, of assets, of navigation and of the environment in the Black Sea," the ministry said in a statement.

The meeting comes after the Turkish-operated container ship Lider Bordo Mavi was struck in the Black Sea on Wednesday, when it was off the coast of Tuapse, Russia.

The Lider Kocatepe was also targeted by a drone when on its way to assist the Lider Bordo Mavi the next day. Turkish media reported that the Lider Bordo Mavi was towed to the Turkish port of Samsun.

Turkiye has been calling for a halt to attacks on civilian vessels in the Black Sea as Ukraine and Russia continue to target each other's export revenues. Navigating the sea has carried heightened risk ever since Russia launched its war on Ukraine in February 2022, but attacks there have escalated.

Several commercial Turkish ships have been hit by drones thought to have been launched by Ukraine. Three crew members were seriously injured when the Nadezhda cargo ship was hit by a drone near the Russian port of Novorossiysk earlier this month.

Turkiye maintains relations with both Moscow and Kyiv, and has positioned itself as a mediator between the two sides. It has not applied Western sanctions on Russia, and has sold US-made defence equipment to Ukraine. A free trade agreement between Turkiye and Ukraine was ratified by the Ukrainian government in July.

However, the issue of safety in the Black Sea is crucial for Turkiye, as its commercial vessels regularly transit the waterway.

Earlier this month, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan called for a halt to attacks in the Black Sea, saying, "They are attacking all commercial shipping without distinction."

articles.title: Milo Yiannopoulos deported to the U.K. one day after ICE arrest
articles.summary: Milo Yiannopoulos, a controversy-baiting internet personality who once vehemently backed President Donald Trump, has been deported to the United Kingdom, a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said on Saturday.
articles.body: Milo Yiannopoulos, a controversy-baiting internet personality who once vehemently backed President Donald Trump, has been deported to the United Kingdom, a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said on Saturday. Yiannopoulos was arrested by ICE at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport on Friday after officials said he failed to show up for an immigration hearing in July. DHS said that a final removal order was issued by an immigration judge on July 22. ICE agents are increasingly making immigration-related arrests at airports. Yiannopoulos, a self-described libertarian who was an early supporter of Trump’s political career, has worked with other MAGA-aligned figures and conspiracy theorists like Ye, formerly Kanye West, since his public parting from Trump’s inner circle. Ye, who has come under fire in recent years for a series of antisemitic statements, performed at the New Orleans Caesars Superdome on Friday evening. It is not clear whether Yiannopoulos was in New Orleans for the concert. Yiannopoulos served as a tech editor at Breitbart, a conservative website, until February 2017, according the site. Yiannopoulos resigned at that time following backlash over comments he’d made suggesting he supported certain adult relationships with children. In those comments, the openly gay agitator discussed the value of “cross-generational relationships.” “And I think particularly in the gay world, and outside the Catholic Church — if that’s where some of you want to go with this — I think in the gay world some of the most important, enriching and incredibly life-affirming, important shaping relationships very often between younger boys and older men,” Yiannopoulos said in a past video clip. “They can be hugely positive experiences.” He also remarked that sexual abuse is “not the worst thing that’s ever going to happen to you ... going bankrupt is worse.” Yiannopoulos was disinvited from speaking at a Conservative Political Action Conference around that time in the wake of those inflammatory remarks. He later apologized and said he didn’t advocate for illegal behavior. He said he was sexually abused himself as a teen by two older men. The Trump administration on Friday publicized Yiannopoulos’ arrest to help promote its voluntary deportation program. DHS is offering undocumented immigrants $3,000 and a free flight home for self-deportation. “Being in detention is a choice,” DHS wrote on X, above Yiannopoulos’ haggard-looking mug shot. “We encourage all illegal aliens to take control of their departure with the [Customs and Border Patrol] Home App.” Conspiracy-peddler Laura Loomer, who is close to Trump and who has claimed responsibility for a number of firings and criminal investigations, took credit for reporting Yiannopoulos to ICE in a social media post.

articles.title: Muslim jail gangs said to force conversions on prisoners in UK: 'Jihadist training camps’
articles.summary: Reports of forced conversions in British prisons have renewed alarm over extremist gang influence. Officials say faith-based coercion will not be tolerated.
articles.body: Radical Muslim inmates are said to be forcing other prisoners — mostly white British men — to convert to Islam in some of the U.K.'s prisons, according to British media reports this week. The problem of Muslim gangs in the nation's prisons has become progressively worse since Britain's Sky News first reported, in 2013, that "British inmates are being bullied into converting to Islam while in jail" while noting that "The Prison Officers Association says it is symptomatic of the growing power and influence of Muslim gangs in prison." This week Nick Timothy, the shadow justice secretary of the opposition Conservative party, has urged the left-of-center Labour Government to root out forced conversions. Timothy posted on X on Tuesday that," Islamist gangs control many of our prisons. Conversion to Islam is the only way to stay safe from them. I obtained data showing 1 in 5 Muslim prisoners are white. That’s four times higher than in the general population. This cannot continue." UK HOME OFFICE GUIDE TELLS ASYLUM SEEKERS NOT TO RAPE, HARASS WOMEN OR MAKE KISSING NOISES He told the U.K.'s Daily Telegraph that "We know that experts have warned repeatedly about forced conversions taking place behind bars, driven by Islamic gangs," Timothy said, adding "We need to be honest that something is not right here – Labour must urgently investigate and stamp out forced conversions in prison." A press release from the U.K. Ministry of Justice stated that, "Most prisons show no evidence of gang-based extremism," while noting "We have also banned terrorist prisoners from holding positions of authority in corporate worship, e.g. leading the call to prayer, and clamped down on material found in prisons that could be used to spread harmful ideologies of justice." According to Nile Gardiner, Director of the Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom at the Heritage Foundation, this growing trend is having a detrimental effect on the country's prison system. "It is an absolutely outrageous state of affairs in the British prison system. This also poses a very significant national security risk for the United Kingdom. articles.title: Centre finalising Article 371 framework for Ladakh, says Rijiju
articles.summary: India News: SRINAGAR: Ladakh is poised for a bespoke constitutional shield, with MHA putting the final touches to a special Article 371 framework for the Union te.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Ladakh is poised for a bespoke constitutional shield, with MHA putting the final touches to a special Article 371 framework for the Union territory, Union minister Kiren Rijiju said.PM Narendra Modi will visit Ladakh to share his views on the proposed framework with people, Rijiju said Friday at a function at Druk Padma Karpo School in Leh district.“Autonomous hill development councils and other existing arrangements are not as empowered. So, recent announcement made by home minister Amit Shah to provide a special provision for Ladakh under Article 371 is going to take shape with the blessings of PM Narendra Modi,” Rijiju said.Unlike Article 370, which gave J&K a high degree of autonomy before its abrogation in 2019, Article 371 provides special, temporary and transitional provisions for balanced regional development and protection of tribal cultures, customary laws and local employment.The proposed Ladakh model is being framed as a “sui generis” governance arrangement. It is expected to offer administrative flexibility and safeguards for tribal land, environment, traditional practices and jobs without granting statehood or directly bringing the region under Sixth Schedule.Rijiju said the provisions would include seven councils, matching Ladakh’s expanded district map. “Earlier, Ladakh had only two districts. Leh and Kargil. Now there are seven districts and along with them there will be seven councils,” he said.Ladakhi representatives from Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the region’s two major political groupings, have been in talks with MHA since 2023 for constitutional safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and environment. Next round of talks is scheduled for Sept in New Delhi.Rijiju said Modi had long believed Ladakh needed special attention and had worked towards its development since taking office in 2014. He said the region’s transformation had been striking, pointing to roads, electricity, water, mobile connectivity and telecommunications that were largely absent a couple of decades ago.“When we were in university, and later when I became an MP in 2004, I came to Ladakh,” he said. “There were no roads, electricity, water or other basic facilities. Today, the situation has changed. With mobile phones available everywhere, vast road network, telecommunication facility, we no longer have to wonder how long it takes to travel from one part of Ladakh to another.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: No place in Hindu thought for excluding Muslims: Bhagwat in New York
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday placed Hindu inclusiveness and society-led political change at the centre of his closely watched addres.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat on Saturday placed Hindu inclusiveness and society-led political change at the centre of his closely watched address at Madison Square Garden, saying a Hindu who wanted India without Muslims would “not remain Hindu” and arguing that public opinion—not political power—was the starting point for lasting change.Bhagwat said the RSS wanted to influence policies, prevent conflicts and “stop wars”, but could not begin by seeking political influence. “Politics has now become a game of self-interest,” he said. Change, he argued, must start in society and create a public view that governments cannot disregard. “If there is public opinion, then no politician will dare to go against it,” he said.Speaking at the “Universal Oneness Celebration” at the Infosys Theatre in Madison Square Garden, Bhagwat said religions were different routes to the same truth. Rituals and religious discipline were necessary, he said, but they should not become more important than the larger goal of reaching the divine.“Diversity is a decoration for our humanity,” he said, adding that it must be “accepted, respected and protected”. While diversity was the rule of nature, unity was the truth behind it, he said.Bhagwat recalled being asked by Muslims during a 2018 lecture series in Delhi whether the RSS’s idea of a Hindu Rashtra meant they would be driven out. “I said, no. That is not Hindu. If any Hindu thinks that there should be no Muslim in Bharat, he will not remain Hindu,” he said. Hindu thought, he added, required acceptance that different paths could lead to the same truth and that every human being had equal dignity.He said the RSS had since continued dialogues with Muslims and Christians, even though results had been slow. Dialogue and service, he said, must proceed together. He cited the organisation’s 1.3 lakh service projects and said assistance was provided without religious discrimination.Bhagwat also addressed questions about the RSS’s public image. The organisation, he said, was once “minuscule” and ignored but had acquired “some say” in Indian society over its 100-year journey. He blamed doubts about it on “wrong narratives” and said they would disappear if people saw the organisation from within.Calling for work at the local level, he asked religious and community leaders to create examples of unity and selfless service in their own countries and gradually take the dialogue to provinces, districts and smaller communities. Changing entrenched attitudes would be “laborious, tedious and time-consuming”, he acknowledged, urging participants not to abandon dialogue because it produced no immediate result. “RSS with all its might is always with you,” he said.The address came after days of controversy around the centenary-year event, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue and supported by more than 200 Hindu American organisations. New York mayor Zohran Mamdani opposed the gathering, describing the RSS’s vision as exclusionary, but acknowledged that the city might not have the authority to cancel a private event.A coalition of civil-rights, interfaith and community groups sought its cancellation, while USCIRF called for Bhagwat’s visa to be revoked and sanctions considered against RSS members. India rejected the commission’s remarks as biased. AHEAD’s X account was briefly suspended and later restored. American singer Mary Millben and BJP spokesperson Nalin Kohli separately criticised Mamdani, arguing that opposing the event contradicted his stated commitment to pluralism.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1997, a woman bought a condemned 1888 San Diego mansion for $188,500; after an 8-year restoration, it has 30-plus chandeliers, a secret bar, ‘Titanic’ movie-set columns and a $4.5 million asking price
articles.summary: US News: In 1997, artist and preservationist Karen Groebli walked into a boarded-up, condemned Victorian mansion in San Diego’s Bankers Hill neighborhood and s.
articles.body: In 1997, artist and preservationist Karen Groebli walked into a boarded-up, condemned Victorian mansion in San Diego’s Bankers Hill neighborhood and saw potential where others saw only ruin. As she later told Homes.com, the plaster was hanging from the walls, original gas lines dangled from the ceiling, broken windows littered the floors and the interior was filled with trash. She bought the 1888 Broderick–Kenny House for $188,500 and spent the next eight years meticulously restoring it, filling the home with more than 30 chandeliers, a hidden speakeasy, and kitchen columns salvaged from the set of James Cameron’s Titanic, according to reporting by Hoodline and local real estate coverage. Now listed for $4.5 million, the house blends historic landmark status with cinematic flair and modern luxury, standing as one of the most unusual entries in San Diego’s current historic home market.From condemned shell to historic landmarkThe Broderick–Kenny House at 2133 2nd Ave. was built during San Diego’s late-19th-century real estate boom and once housed the city’s first music school. It even featured one of the city’s earliest residential water-pressure elevators, which Groebli later restored and reimagined using an antique cab and scissor gates.By the time Groebli found it in 1997, however, the house had been declared condemned, repeatedly vandalised and stripped of nearly all its interior character. “Whatever could have possibly been nice in that house had literally just been torn from the walls,” Groebli told Homes.com. “The plaster was just hanging; it was all over the floor. The original gas lines in the ceiling were bent and hanging out. The windows were broken. It was filled with trash.”Despite the damage, she felt an immediate connection, shaped in part by childhood visits to a modest Victorian her great-grandfather built by hand in Northern California in 1903. “It was just an immediate attraction,” she said. “We needed each other.”The house already carried formal protection: the City of San Diego Historical Resources Board designated it as San Diego Historic Landmark #136 on May 4, 1979, roughly two decades before Groebli’s restoration began.An eight-year labour of loveGroebli’s first task was to undo decades of ill-advised alterations: drop ceilings with acoustic tiles, cheap partition walls, missing molding and other “horrible things that people had added on over the years,” she told Homes.com. Once those were removed, she worked to recreate the home’s original floor plan, respecting its unusually large, bold Victorian layout.“This Victorian is different than others in that it has a lot of rooms, and they’re on a larger scale,” Groebli explained. “A lot of Victorians are more filled with secret passages and tiny doors, but this house was bigger and bolder in its design from the beginning, so I wanted to stick with that. I wanted it to have a more eclectic feel.”Over eight years, she lived and breathed the restoration, hand-sourcing era-specific furniture and decor with a clear plan for each room. “I basically would haunt all the local salvage and antique stores,” she said, as per the report. “I had a notebook where I kept a reference of everything. If I bought a chandelier, I’d note that it was going in bedroom two, and then I’d know I still needed one for bedroom four.”Titanic columns and a Wyatt Earp-linked speakeasyThat method led to some of the home’s most talked-about features. Four decorative columns in the kitchen were salvaged from the set of Titanic, where they were built as exact replicas of the ocean liner’s actual first-class dining room columns. Groebli learned about them through her car mechanic, whose wife was an extra in the film and knew someone selling set pieces.“The minute I saw those four columns, I just imagined them in the kitchen, and they turned out really cool,” she said. Because the columns had been underwater with the set, they required extensive restoration and “tons of sanding,” but they now stand as a centrepiece of the kitchen.Another standout is the hidden speakeasy, tucked behind antique stained-glass French doors that once hung inside the Tivoli Bar and Grill, a Gaslamp Quarter establishment founded in 1885 and famously frequented by frontier lawman Wyatt Earp. Those original entry doors now lead into the home’s private bar, adding a layer of Wild West history to the Victorian bones.Modern luxury layered onto 1888 bonesThe restored Broderick–Kenny House spans 4,500 square feet with four bedrooms and five bathrooms, blending its 1888 structure with modern updates throughout. Groebli added a custom freestanding steel spiral staircase and converted the entire third floor into a primary suite with private observation decks overlooking San Diego Bay, the downtown skyline and the Coronado Bridge.The home includes more than 30 chandeliers, custom sconces, multiple decks and panoramic skyline views, according to local coverage. Compass agent Lindsay Dunlap, who holds the listing, told Fox 5 San Diego and KUSI News that buyers can purchase the home furnished or bundled with an adjacent three-unit building.A $4.5 million outlier in Bankers HillAt $4.5 million, the Broderick–Kenny House sits well above typical Bankers Hill home values. Single-family homes in the neighborhood posted a year-to-date median sale price of $1,751,069 in early 2026, according to San Diego Association of REALTORS market statistics, making the listing a significant outlier even in a neighborhood known for its historic housing stock.It isn’t the only high-end historic property on the block, though. A neighbouring eight-bedroom estate at 2115 2nd Avenue was listed for $6.5 million in August, pointing to a growing cluster of multimillion-dollar historic homes along the 2nd Avenue corridor.Dunlap described the current San Diego market as “quirky,” with buyers more cautious and specific about what they want. “We’re looking for someone who’s looking for a collector’s item — a house collector of sorts,” she told Homes.com. “This isn’t your average family home. It certainly could be, but I think we’re looking for someone who appreciates the restoration and preservation.”Victorians are relatively rare in San Diego, with only about two selling in a typical year, and even fewer in urban neighborhoods like Bankers Hill. “That’s what makes it so special,” Dunlap said.A financial perk for the next ownerThe home’s historic designation also comes with a practical benefit. The property benefits from California’s Mills Act historic preservation program, which offers local tax reductions ranging from 20% to 70% in exchange for maintaining the home’s historic architectural integrity, according to Save Our Heritage Organisation. The Mills Act tax contract automatically transfers to new buyers, meaning whoever closes on the Broderick–Kenny House inherits the savings along with the address.A preservationist’s next chapterFor Groebli, the sale marks the end of a nearly three-decade chapter that began with a condemned shell and a vision. She bought the house for $188,500 in 1997, invested eight years of intensive restoration, and lived in the home while continuing to refine its details. Now she is moving on to her next project, leaving behind a one-of-a-kind Victorian that blends San Diego history, Hollywood memorabilia and her own eclectic design sensibility.For the right buyer, the Broderick–Kenny House offers more than square footage and views; it offers a story—of decay and rebirth, of salvage and cinema, and of one woman’s determination to bring a forgotten mansion back to life.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Quote of the day by Brock Lesnar: "Nobody likes to lose, and I'm a sore loser, especially when…" - why losing can hurt even more when you blame yourself
articles.summary: US News: Brock Lesnar's quote offers a genuinely candid look at the competitive mindset that can make defeat considerably harder to accept than it might first .
articles.body: Brock Lesnar's quote offers a genuinely candid look at the competitive mindset that can make defeat considerably harder to accept than it might first appear. "Nobody likes to lose, and I'm a sore loser," he said, "especially when I feel I gave the first fight to him." This line is documented directly on UFC.com, in an official piece titled "Flashback – The Quotable Mr. Lesnar," dated to 2009 and specifically noted as something he said before his rematch with Frank Mir. Lesnar had lost his actual UFC debut to Mir at UFC 81, submitted in the first round by a kneebar, a genuinely painful way to lose your very first fight in a brand new sport. His words capture something considerably deeper than simply disliking defeat in general. Feeling that you personally gave a fight away creates a genuinely sharper kind of frustration, since it suggests the outcome was actually within your own control all along.Quote of the day by Brock Lesnar"Nobody likes to lose, and I'm a sore loser, especially when I feel I gave the (first) fight to him"What actually happened between these two fightsThe real story behind this quote makes it considerably more interesting than a simple general statement about losing. After that first-round submission loss to Mir at UFC 81, Lesnar spent months working toward a genuine rematch, which finally arrived at UFC 100, one of the most significant events in UFC history. He won that rematch decisively, via TKO in the second round. What happened immediately afterwards became almost as famous as the fight itself. During his post-fight interview with Joe Rogan, Lesnar delivered a genuinely controversial, heavily criticised rant aimed partly at event sponsors and partly at Mir himself, behaviour that the UFC's own leadership was clearly unhappy about. At the actual post-fight press conference, Lesnar apologised directly, repeating almost the same sentiment as today's quote. "I'm a sore loser," he admitted again, "so when I won tonight I just let my emotions get the better of me... the only thing I truly had against him was he beat me." That repetition across two separate moments shows this was never really a passing comment. It reflected something genuinely consistent about how Lesnar actually experienced both losing and winning.What the quote by Brock Lesnar genuinely meansAt its simplest, Lesnar is acknowledging something a great many competitive people genuinely experience, that losing hurts considerably more when you honestly believe you could have performed better yourself. There is a real difference between losing because an opponent was simply better on the day, and losing while genuinely feeling that your own mistakes contributed heavily to the actual result. The second kind of defeat tends to leave a person replaying the situation over and over, quietly wondering what they should have done differently instead.Why losing can genuinely be so difficult to acceptCompetition naturally creates a real desire to win. When someone trains, prepares and genuinely commits themselves to a specific goal, losing can feel like considerably more than just a disappointing result on its own. It can feel like all of that preparation simply failed to produce the outcome they actually wanted. For genuinely competitive people, that frustration can become especially intense, and the emotional reaction to losing can actually reveal a great deal about how much someone genuinely cares about what they are trying to accomplish in the first place.What "I gave the fight to him" genuinely meansLesnar's phrase suggests he believed his own performance had genuinely contributed to his opponent's victory, rather than simply being outclassed entirely. That can be one of the genuinely hardest forms of defeat to actually accept. If someone else simply outperforms you cleanly, there is a fairly clear lesson available, that they were better on that particular occasion. When your own hesitation or poor decisions genuinely influence the result instead, the loss can start to feel entirely avoidable, which stings in a considerably different way. That frustration becomes genuinely useful only if it eventually leads to honest self-evaluation, rather than simply curdling into blame directed elsewhere.Why genuinely competitive people can struggle so much with defeatCompetitive personalities often set extremely high standards for themselves, and winning naturally reinforces those standards over time. Losing can therefore create a genuinely sharp contrast between what someone expected of themselves and what actually happened on the day. The instinct in that moment may well be to become angry or visibly disappointed, exactly as Lesnar's own post-fight behaviour at UFC 100 demonstrated. The genuinely important question is always what happens next. A competitive person can let that frustration consume them entirely, or they can use it as real motivation to identify a genuine weakness and actually improve it.Why losing never has to mean genuine failureA loss is simply an outcome. It is never automatically a final judgement on someone's actual ability. Even elite athletes lose regularly, Lesnar himself among them. The real difference between a temporary setback and something closer to lasting failure usually comes down to what a person genuinely does afterwards. Reviewing honest mistakes, adjusting real preparation, and returning with a genuinely better strategy can turn an unpleasant result into something considerably more useful, actual experience worth having.Why real accountability is genuinely part of competitionLesnar's quote also contains a real element of personal accountability worth noticing. If you genuinely believe you contributed to your own defeat, acknowledging that honestly tends to be considerably more productive than simply blaming circumstances or other people instead. Taking real responsibility does not mean ignoring an opponent's own role in the result. It means being genuinely honest about your own performance, which is exactly what can identify the specific areas that actually need improvement afterwards.How to handle losing like a genuine competitorAllow yourself to feel genuinely disappointed, since losing can hurt, and pretending otherwise rarely makes it any easier.Review honestly what actually happened, separating real emotion from an accurate assessment of your own performance.Take real responsibility for the mistakes that were genuinely within your control.Give proper credit to your opponent too, since their performance is also genuinely part of the reason you lost.Avoid making excuses, since honest explanations are useful, but excuses rarely actually lead to improvement.Identify one genuinely clear lesson, since every defeat can reveal something specific that still needs work.Turn real frustration into preparation, using disappointment as genuine motivation for the next challenge ahead.Do not let a single result define you entirely, since one loss does not erase everything you achieved before it.Focus your effort where the defeat genuinely exposed a real gap in your ability.Come back properly prepared, since the strongest response to a disappointing result is very often simply a better performance next time.What it means in today's worldNobody genuinely enjoys losing, yet the hardest defeats can sometimes teach the most useful lessons. When someone honestly believes they could have performed better themselves, real disappointment can become a genuine opportunity to examine their own decisions, preparation and mindset properly. Lesnar's blunt admission, repeated across two separate moments of his own career, captures the emotional side of competition honestly, while still pointing toward something genuinely valuable, that you cannot actually change a result once it has happened, but you can genuinely decide what that loss ends up teaching you. A real competitive spirit was never simply about wanting to win. It is just as much about being genuinely willing to confront your own mistakes, learn honestly from defeat, and return properly determined to perform better next time.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
